item.title: This Week in Spring - November 18th, 2026
item.dc:creator: joshlong
item.content:encoded:
Hi, Spring fans! Welcome to another installment of This Week in Spring! I've literally just touched down in gorgeous Thessaloniki, Greece for the Voxxed Days Thessaloniki event. I'm so excited!

We've got a ton of stuff to look into, then.. I'm headed to bed! Got an amazing day of podcasts this week, so be sure to check out the channel!

Let's dive into it!

  • first thing's first: UPDATE YOUR JVMs! The new Java4Shell CVE looks pretty nasty.
  • announcing a new home for Spring for Apache Pulsar
  • I loved recording this discussion with James Ward at AGNTCon 2026 with Alexander Ioffe
  • and this one, also with James Ward, talking to Ben Hale](AGNTCon 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n6PFNJBol70)
  • in last week's installment of A Bootiful Podcast, I had the privilege of talking to Atomikos founder Guy Pardon
  • Spring AI 2.1.0-RC2 available now
  • Spring Boot 4.2.0-RC2 available now
  • Spring Cloud 2026.0.0-RC1 (aka Paddington) has been released
  • it was a lot of fun to be on the Spring Office Hours podcast with DaShaun, chatting with Corby Page

item.title: Spring Office Hours Podcast: S5E30 - What’s New in IntelliJ IDEA and AIR with Anton Arhipov
item.dc:creator: danvega
item.content:encoded:
Join Dan Vega and DaShaun Carter for the latest updates from the Spring Ecosystem. This week, Dan and DaShaun are joined by Anton Arhipov from JetBrains to talk about what’s new in IntelliJ IDEA and AIR. They look at the latest features for Java and Spring developers, how AIR fits into your workflow, and the tips that will save you time every day. Bring your IntelliJ questions. You can join the live stream to ask questions or catch the replay on your favorite podcast platform.

Show Notes

  • JetBrains Air and Air in JetBrains IDEs
  • What's New in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 and the What's New video
  • Logpoints in IntelliJ IDEA
  • Java and Kotlin by IntelliJ IDEA for VS Code and Cursor (IntelliJ IDEA goes LSP)
  • Spring release calendar
  • Secure All The Things! (With Spring Security) by Josh Long, free on Leanpub
  • Anton Arhipov on X and LinkedIn

The show:

  • springofficehours.io - episodes, schedule, community
  • Spring Developer on YouTube - join us live every Monday
  • Dan Vega
  • DaShaun Carter
  • The Spring Blog - the news we cover each week

item.title: A Bootiful Podcast: Atomikos founder Guy Pardon on distributed transactions, data integrity, and more
item.dc:creator: joshlong
item.content:encoded:
Hi, Spring fans! Tired of worrying whether your data is actually correct? In this episode, we dive into the world of distributed transactions with Guy Pardon, founder of Atomikos, and unpack the technology that keeps mission-critical systems consistent when one database, one message broker, or one service call just isn’t enough.

If you’ve ever wondered how banks move money safely, how insurance systems protect claim data, or how modern Spring apps can get enterprise-grade transaction guarantees without an application server, this conversation is for you. We explore why XA still matters, how two-phase commit really works, when you should use distributed transactions, and why compensating logic and “eventually consistent” workarounds aren’t always enough.

We also talk about Atomikos itself: the open source core, the premium observability and support features, cloud-friendly log storage, Spring Boot integration, and how it helps teams build reliable systems that just work. If you care about data integrity, resilience, and making sure “committed” really means committed, don’t miss this one.

item.title: Announcing a New Home for Spring for Apache Pulsar
item.dc:creator: jasonkonicki
item.content:encoded:
We are excited to announce an important transition for the Spring for Apache Pulsar project! To foster even deeper integration and collaboration with the broader Pulsar community, the project is moving to a new official home as a subproject within the Apache Pulsar project at the Apache Software Foundation.

Going forward, the subproject will be officially named Apache Pulsar support for Spring.

Why the Move?

Since its inception, Spring for Apache Pulsar has helped developers seamlessly build reactive and message-driven applications using Spring paradigms alongside Apache Pulsar's powerful messaging features. Bringing this integration directly into the Apache Pulsar project allows the community to streamline development, accelerate feature support, and ensure long-term alignment with the evolution of Apache Pulsar.

Important Maintenance & Support Information

As part of this transition:

  • Final Release: Spring for Apache Pulsar 2.0.8 is the final release under the Spring project umbrella.
  • End of Maintenance: The Spring team will no longer publish updates, maintenance patches, or bug fixes for Spring for Apache Pulsar within existing or future active Spring release trains.
  • New Support Model: All ongoing maintenance, feature development, bug fixes, project support, and releases will now be handled directly by the Apache Pulsar project.

Spring Boot Starter and Spring Cloud Stream Binder

This transition also affects related ecosystem integrations:

  • Spring Boot Starter: We will discontinue maintenance of the Spring Boot starter for Spring Pulsar. Version 2.0.8 will remain available with Spring Boot 4.2.0. For subsequent releases, users should switch to the starter provided by the new Apache Pulsar support for Spring project.
  • Spring Cloud Stream Binder: The Spring Cloud Stream binder for Apache Pulsar will also migrate. Spring Cloud Stream will include the Pulsar binder in its upcoming 5.1.0 release. Following that release, users should obtain the binder directly from the Apache Pulsar support for Spring project.

What's Next for Developers?

Existing applications can safely continue using version 2.0.8 (and the 5.1.0 binder in Spring Cloud Stream). However, to receive future updates, bug fixes, and new features, developers will need to transition their dependency coordinates and package imports to align with the new project under Apache Pulsar.

Thank You!

We want to extend our heartfelt gratitude to everyone who contributed to, tested, and used Spring for Apache Pulsar. We look forward to seeing the project continue to thrive in its new home within the Apache Pulsar community!

For more details, check out the official announcement blog post from the Apache Pulsar project.
